h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר מ״א Pesach — Maamar Mem Aleph

p: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל הָעָם: אַל תִּירָאוּ, הִתְיַצְבוּ וּרְאוּ אֶת יְשׁוּעַת ה' וְגוֹמֵר
"And Moshe said to the people: 'Do not fear; stand firm (hisyatzvu) and see the salvation of Hashem, etc.'"
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, י"ג).
(Shemos 14:13).
מַהוּ הַלָּשׁוֹן "הִתְיַצְבוּ"?
What is the meaning of the expression "stand firm" (hisyatzvu)?
אַךְ הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
Indeed, it is along the lines of what they said
(תַּנְחוּמָא נִצָּבִים א'):
(Tanchuma Nitzavim 1):
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקְּלָלוֹת הַלָּלוּ בָּאוֹת עֲלֵיכֶם הֵן מַעֲמִידִים אֶתְכֶם וְכוּלֵּי, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים וְגוֹמֵר.
"Even though these curses come upon you, they cause you to stand upright and endure, etc.; therefore it is said, 'You are standing firm (nitzavim), etc.'"
וְכֵן אָמַר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה: אַל תִּירָאוּ—שֶׁהַיִּרְאָה הִיא נוֹתֶנֶת לָכֶם עֲמִידָה וְקִיּוּם,
And similarly Moshe said to them: "Do not fear [the Egyptians]"—for the awe [of Hashem] gives you standing and endurance,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and as it is said
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, י'):
(Shemos 14:10):
וּפַרְעֹה הִקְרִיב,
"And Pharaoh drew near (hikriv),"
וְאִיתָא
and it is stated
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ה' וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב' מ"ז.)
(Shemos Rabbah 21:5 and holy Zohar, Vol. 2, 47a)
שֶׁהִקְרִיב לִבָּם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִתְשׁוּבָה
that he drew the hearts of Israel near to repentance
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: הִתְיַצְבוּ, וּמִזּוֹ הַיִּרְאָה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם עֲמִידָה וּמַצֵּבָה וּרְאוּ אֶת יְשׁוּעַת ה' וְגוֹמֵר.
and this is why it says "stand firm": out of this awe you will gain standing and stability, "and see the salvation of Hashem, etc."
לֹא תֹסִיפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עַד עוֹלָם
"You shall see them no more until eternity (ad olam)"
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' נ"ג:)
הִקְשָׁה: הָא כְּתִיב: וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מִצְרַיִם מֵת וְגוֹמֵר!
it asks: Surely it is written afterward, "And Israel saw Egypt dead [upon the seashore], etc."!

אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מֵתִין חֲמוּ לְהוּ. אָמַר לֵיהּ: אִי כְּתִיב "לֹא תֹסִיפוּ לִרְאֹתָם חַיִּים" הֲוָה אָמֵינָא הָכִי וְכוּלֵּי; אֶלָּא תָּא חֲזֵי: כְּתִיב: מִן הָעוֹלָם וְעַד הָעוֹלָם, וּתְנֵינַן: עוֹלָם לְעֵילָּא וְעוֹלָם לְתַתָּא וְכוּלֵּי—עַד עוֹלָם: עַד דְּיִתְּעַר הַאי עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי.

"Rabbi Yossi said: They saw them dead. He replied to him: Had it been written 'You shall see them no more alive,' I would say so, etc.; rather, come and see: it is written 'from the world and unto the world,' and we have learned there is an Upper World and a Lower World, etc.—'until eternity (ad olam)' means until that Supernal World awakens, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ דִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף בְּעַתִּיקָא תַּלְיָא
That is, the Splitting of the Sea depends upon Atika
(זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם נ"ב:),
(holy Zohar, ibid. 52b),
וְהַיְינוּ כָּל שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁקָּרָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת דְּעַתִּיקָא
which encompasses all the first three Sefiros, just as the holy Zohar calls the Shabbos daytime meal "the meal of Atika"
(שָׁם פ"ח.)
(ibid. 88a)
וּבְרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא קְרָאוֹ שַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה
and in Ra'aya Mehemna calls it "the Supernal Shabbos"
(ibid. 92a),
וְהַיְינוּ בִּינָה, וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא
which is Binah, along the lines of what is brought
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא חֵלֶק ג' רנ"ז.):
(Ra'aya Mehemna, Vol. 3, 257a):
אֲבָל מִבִּינָה וּלְעֵילָּא אִיהִי מְנוּחָה וְעוֹנֶג וּשְׁבִיתָה לְכָל עוֹבָדָא
"Whereas from Binah and above, there is rest, delight, and cessation from all labor"
וּכְשֶׁזּוֹכִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה שֶׁהִיא בִּינָה, זוֹכִין גַּם כֵּן לְחָכְמָה, דְּחָכְמָה וּבִינָה תְּרֵין רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין לְעָלְמִין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר
and when Israel merit the Supernal Shabbos, which is Binah, they simultaneously merit Chochmah, for Chochmah and Binah are "two companions that never separate," as brought in the Zohar
וּמֵחִיבּוּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה, מוֹחָא וְלִיבָּא, מוֹלִיד הַדַּעַת שֶׁהִיא פְּנִימִיּוּת מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן—וְזֶה "עַד עוֹלָם", שֶׁהוּא קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף שֶׁהָיָה בְּעַתִּיקָא.

and from the union of Chochmah and Binah—mind and heart—is born Da'as, which is the inwardness of Kesser Elyon; and this is "until that World," which was the Splitting of the Sea taking place in Atika.
וְזֶה שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: כְּדֵין כְּתִיב: וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּה' וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ
And this is what is brought in the holy Zohar: "Then it is written, 'And they believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant'"
דְּאַף דְּמִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה אִיהִי אֱמוּנָה
for even though the final attribute [Malchus] is Faith
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא שָׁם ר"ל.)
(Ra'aya Mehemna, ibid. 230a)
וְכֵן אִיהִי יִרְאָה וְשַׁרְיָא בַּהּ יִרְאָה
and likewise "She is fear and fear rests upon her"
(זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק א' ה':),
(holy Zohar, Vol. 1, 5b),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שְׁלֵימוּת הָאֱמוּנָה הוּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא
nevertheless the perfection of faith is in the revelation of Atika, as brought
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' פ"ח.)
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 88a)
דְּהָא תַּלְיָא מְהֵימְנוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא בְּעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא וְכוּלֵּי, הַיְינוּ אֱמוּנָה יְתֵירָה
that supernal faith depends on Atika Kadisha, etc., which is surpassing faith
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ל"ז),
(as explained in Maamar 37),
וְכֵן אַף דְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּת הִיא יִרְאָה וְנִקְרָא לֵב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
and likewise even though the attribute of Malchus is fear and is called "heart," as they said
(יוֹמָא ע"ב:)
(Yoma 72b)
עַל מִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם: "וְלֶב אָיִן",
regarding one who lacks fear of Heaven, "'And he has no heart,'"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בִּינָה לִיבָּא, הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנָס הַיִּרְאָה לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
nevertheless Binah is the true inner heart, meaning when fear enters the very depths of the heart, as it is said
(Mishlei 2:5):
אָז תָּבִין יִרְאַת ה'.
"Then you will understand (tavin) the fear of Hashem."

וְלָכֵן בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף כְּתִיב: וַיִּירְאוּ הָעָם אֶת ה' וַיַּאֲמִינוּ, שֶׁאָז זָכוּ לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּרְאָה וְהָאֱמוּנָה וְהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא, וְזֶהוּ: לֹא תֹסִיפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עוֹד עַד עוֹלָם, ה' יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם וְגוֹמֵר.

Therefore, at the Splitting of the Sea it is written "And the people feared Hashem and believed," for then they merited the perfection of awe, faith, and the revelation of Atika—and this is "You shall see them no more until eternity; Hashem will fight for you, etc."
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר "ה' יִלְחוֹם לָכֶם"!
Now Scripture should have said yichlom ("will fight," active) rather than yilacheim (passive/reflexive)!
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁהִקְשָׁה בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
However, the explanation follows what the holy Zohar asked
(חֵלֶק ב' נ"ו.):
כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב: ה' אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה, לָא יָדַעְנָא דַּה' שְׁמוֹ?!
"Once it is written 'Hashem is a man of war,' do I not know that Hashem is His Name?!"
אַךְ בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף הָיָה קִטְרוּגִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
Rather, at the Splitting of the Sea there were heavenly prosecutions, as they said in the Midrash
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ז')
(Shemos Rabbah 21:7)
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ק"ע:);

אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁזָּכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא, דְּהַיְינוּ לְכָל קְדוּשַּׁת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַתֵּשַׁע מִדּוֹת—י"ה חָכְמָה וּבִינָה, ו' הַמִּדּוֹת, ה' מַלְכוּת, וְתָגוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְכֶתֶר עֶלְיוֹן בְּסוֹד הַדַּעַת—וְאָז נַעֲשָׂה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה;

yet once Israel merited the revelation of Atika—meaning the full holiness of the Name Havayah encompassing all nine attributes (Yud-Hei Chochmah and Binah, Vav the six attributes, Hei Malchus, and the tip of the Yud alluding to Kesser Elyon in the secret of Da'as)—then Hashem, may He be blessed, became, as it were, a "man of war";
דִּבְלֹא זֶה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹהֵב מִשְׁפָּט וְלֹא יָכוֹל לִדְחוֹת הַמְּקַטְרְגִים,
for without this, Hashem, may He be blessed, "loves justice" and could not dismiss the prosecuting angels,
אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁזָּכוּ לִקְדוּשַּׁת עַתִּיקָא, שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְשׁוּרִים בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ בַּה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
but once they merited the holiness of Atika—recognizing that Israel are bound at their root to Hashem, may He be blessed, as they said
(בְּרָכוֹת י"ז.):
(Berachos 17a):
גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה וְכוּלֵּי,
"It is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will, and what prevents us? The leaven in the dough, etc.,"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַמִּצְרִים הֵם הַחַיָּיבִים בְּכָל חַטָּאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל—וְאָז נַעֲשָׂה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה.
meaning the Egyptians are the ones culpable for all of Israel's sins—then Hashem, may He be blessed, became a man of war.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ה' יִלָּחֵם — שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה, וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִישׁוּן וַדַּאי
And this is what is said: "Hashem will make Himself into a warrior (yilacheim)"—He will become a man of war—"and you shall surely remain silent"
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּשַׁלַּח מַאֲמָר י').
(as explained in Beshalach, Maamar 10).
וְזֶה זָכוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁקָּפְצוּ לַיָּם בִּמְסִירוּת נֶפֶשׁ עַל אֱמוּנַת ה', וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
And this they merited because they plunged into the sea with self-sacrifice out of faith in Hashem, as they said in the Gemara
(סוֹטָה ל"ז.)
(Sotah 37a)
וּבַמְּכִילְתָּא
and in the Mechilta
(Beshalach 5)
שֶׁבָּאוּ עַד חוֹטְמָן בַּמַּיִם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְהִתְגַּלּוּת וְלִקְדוּשַּׁת כָּל שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה כָּאָמוּר.
that they entered the water up to their nostrils, and through this they merited the revelation and holiness of the entire Name Havayah, as stated.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיִּסָּעוּ
And this is what is meant by "And they shall journey forward"
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
for in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' מ"ח.)
מַקְשֶׁה: וְכִי לְאָן אֲתַר פְּקִיד לוֹן דִּינְטְלוּן וְכוּלֵּי? אֶלָּא אַהְדַּר לְעֵילָּא וְכוּלֵּי
it asks: "To what place did He command them to journey [when the sea stood before them], etc.? Rather, it turns upward [to the supernal flow], etc."
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא מִקּוֹדֵם: "אֵלַי" דַּיְיקָא, וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
which is like what is brought earlier, "'unto Me (eilai)' specifically," and in the holy Zohar
(שָׁם קע"ח:):
(ibid. 178b):
"אֵלַי" דַּיְיקָא וְכוּלֵּי, "וַיִּסָּעוּ" דַּיְיקָא בְּמַזָּלָא הֲוָה תָּלוּי וְכוּלֵּי
"'unto Me' specifically, etc.; 'and they shall journey'—specifically upon the supernal Mazal [Atika] did it depend, etc."

meaning that then Israel merited to be "My firstborn son," children to Hashem, and as the Rama of Fano, of blessed memory, wrote, "The soul of a father is the mazal for the son," which is the root of his soul;

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShemesh, Beshalach — “A person should fear nothing but Hashem; all fears exist only to rouse him to the fear of His exaltedness, and one who has it cannot be ruled by anything frightening. When Israel left Egypt they came to great attachment to Hashem; but when outer fear came upon them, they saw that they were not yet attached. This is ‘And Pharaoh drew near… and they feared greatly’: when they saw that they feared Egypt, they cried out to Hashem, that is, they repented for having an outer fear. Therefore Moshe told them, ‘Stand firm… Hashem will fight for you and you shall be silent’: come to great attachment, almost a nullification of being.” Connection: The Maor VaShemesh likewise reads ‘do not fear’ as the replacement of fear of Egypt by fear of Heaven, prompted by Pharaoh's drawing them to repentance, and adds that it issues in an attachment that leaves nothing to fear.

At the Splitting of the Sea there was prosecution, only it depended on Atika. ‘Hashem is a man of war’: ‘ish’ indicates the three first Sefiros; and this is ‘Hashem is His Name,’ for then the aspect of ‘He’ was revealed, as in the future, when ‘Hashem will be One and His Name One.’” Connection: The same link between the revelation of Atika that overcame the prosecution and “Hashem, a man of war”; it reads the word “ish” itself as the three upper Sefiros and the Sea as a foretaste of the future unity of the Name.

paragraphs.text: Mechilta, Beshalach (Vayehi) 6 [5 in some editions] — "While they stood taking counsel, Nachshon ben Aminadav jumped and fell into the waves of the sea. Of him it says, 'Save me, O God, for the waters have come up to the soul; I am sunk in the deep mire.' At that moment the Omnipresent said to Moshe: My beloved one is drowning in the water, the sea is closing in, and you stand and prolong your prayer?"

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 48a (Beshalach) — "'Speak to the children of Israel and let them travel': … Where did He command them to travel? They were camped by the sea! Rather, He went back up, as it is written, 'Why do you cry out to Me (elai)?' — for all of it stands in that place. Therefore 'let them travel' — let them move away from this, for this is not the time."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 178b (Sifra DiTzniusa, ch. 4) — "'Why do you cry out to Me (elai)?' — 'to Me' precisely. 'Speak to the children of Israel and let them travel' — 'let them travel' precisely. It depended on the mazal [the supernal beard], for He wished to honor His beard."
